page: Hetzner Cloud cax31 is an Arm-based virtual server deployed on the QEMU hypervisor within the vendor's Cost Optimized family. The instance is powered by an Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 2.0 GHz, offering 8 vCPUs backed by 8 physical cores with single-thread-per-core execution and shared CPU scheduling. Hardware resources include 16.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 1.95 GB of RAM per vCPU, paired with 160 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The configuration includes zero dedicated GPUs and does not bundle complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate steady multi-core efficiency alongside modest single-thread execution. The server achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1029.0 and a multi-core score of 5619.0, complemented by a multi-core stress-ng rating of 14164.78. Memory bandwidth reaches 75.87 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and 32.14 GB/sec on writes. In operational tests, cax31 handles 9.74 million Redis SET operations per second and achieves a static web serving throughput of 7.92 GB/sec. Extended software compilation using Clang measures at 8251.0, while decompression and text processing metrics remain comparatively weak.

With a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation and shared compute architecture, cax31 offers resource efficiency for concurrent processing workloads that do not require dedicated core isolation or vector acceleration extensions like AVX or AMX. The instance delivers steady utility for multi-threaded web hosting, continuous integration build runners, microservice application backends, and distributed caching tiers.
description: Hetzner Cloud cax31 is an Arm-based cloud server powered by an 8-vCPU Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 2.0 GHz with shared core allocation. The hardware configuration bundles 16.0 GB of memory (1.95 GB per core) and 160 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, without a dedicated GPU or complimentary public IPv4 address. Benchmarks highlight moderate multi-threaded efficiency, posting a Geekbench multi-core score of 5619.0 and achieving 9.74 million Redis SET operations per second alongside 7.92 GB/sec of static web serving throughput. However, its single-core metrics remain modest, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1029.0 and slower compression processing. The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio presents a cost-effective environment for scalable multi-threaded tasks, making cax31 well aligned with general web serving, software compilation, CI/CD runners, and distributed container microservices where high single-threaded performance or vector acceleration is not strictly required.
